title: [VSC-8] VS Code: Delivery section in task detail from the shared delivery corpus
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). Depends on VSC-3 (task-a5f39d5535404f6e9e59f762c046f5e0), which lands moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-delivery.json. This row must pass that corpus UNCHANGED: it is a held-out test, and QA rejects a diff that edits it. A row VS Code cannot meet because JetBrains is wrong is filed against JetBrains, never edited.

Objective: JetBrains' task detail shows a Delivery section (DeliveryPresentation.kt, MoeBundle keys moe.delivery.*): candidate SHA and base, the runner-reported check (command, exit-code verdict, outcome, source), whether the required check counted by policy, the reported delivery target and landed revision, and the owning attempt phase. The daemon serves it as task.delivery on /ws (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts, deliveryProjection from packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.ts). VS Code drops it: src/types/moe.ts has no delivery type and TaskDetailPanel.ts renders nothing.

Deliverable:
- moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts: the TaskDelivery shape (type-only; transpileModule elides it).
- moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts: an exported `deliveryRows(delivery)` returning `{ labelKey, value, fullValue, outcome }[]` with JetBrains' semantics; a `DELIVERY_LABELS` map from labelKey to English; and a Delivery section (title from moe.delivery.title) rendered with escapeHtml, PASS and FAIL styled, the full value in a title attribute, nothing rendered when the list is empty. Keep this code inside TaskDetailPanel.ts: three peer test files load the panel under node:vm with a strict require map, so a new value import breaks them (mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map).
- new moe-vscode/tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs: loads the corpus via `path.join(__dirname, '../../moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-delivery.json')`, checks deliveryRows against every row (all failing ids reported together), checks DELIVERY_LABELS against the moe.delivery.* values parsed from moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties (VSC-0's shared-strings rule), and renders one populated and one null delivery through the real panel HTML (fake webview, pattern in tests/task-blocker-visibility.test.cjs).

TaskDetailPanel.ts is shared with VSC-9 and VSC-11: in shared-checkout mode do not run concurrently with them; after this project's worktree switch they merge independently.

Not in scope: the board card, commit and landing lists, verification evidence, any moe-jetbrains file, the corpus.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo (the test reads moe-jetbrains files) into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
definitionOfDone: moe-vscode/tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs runs every row of moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-delivery.json through TaskDetailPanel's exported deliveryRows and passes, reporting all failing ids at once.
The same test asserts DELIVERY_LABELS equals the moe.delivery.* entries parsed from moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties.
The rendered task-detail HTML for a populated delivery holds the Delivery title and one escaped row per expected entry in corpus order; for a null delivery it holds no Delivery section.

implementationPlan.description:
Write the consumer test moe-vscode/tests/delivery-corpus.test.cjs FIRST, with the Write tool; it stays red until steps 2-3 land. Copy the harness shape of tests/task-blocker-visibility.test.cjs into this file (transpile, strict, loadModule, fakeVscode, panelDependencies with `vscode` and `./PlanReviewPanel`, renderDetail through TaskDetailPanel.createOrShow with a strict client stub and dispose in finally, and a makeTask fixture like its own). Never require that test file (mem:convention-vscode-renderer-tests, mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map). The corpus is `path.join(__dirname, '../../moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-delivery.json')`, landed by VSC-3 (task-a5f39d55, plan revision 1): `{ version: 1, rows: [ { id, note, delivery, expect: [ { labelKey, value, fullValue, outcome } ] } ] }`, 16 rows D01..D16, and every expect entry spells all four members with outcome 'PASS', 'FAIL' or null. Never edit the corpus or any moe-jetbrains file. Its error handling: an unreadable or unparseable corpus or MoeBundle.properties fails with a message naming the path; every per-row check collects `: ...` messages and ends in one assert, so all failing ids show at once. Tests: 1. `every corpus row renders through deliveryRows`: version 1 and at least 12 rows. For each row compare `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(panel.deliveryRows(row.delivery)))` with row.expect using util.isDeepStrictEqual. The JSON round trip strips vm-realm prototypes, and it drops an undefined outcome so that one cannot pass for null. Collect `": expected , got "` and finish with one assert.deepStrictEqual(failures, []). 2. `DELIVERY_LABELS equals the bundle's moe.delivery.* entries`: parse moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties with `/^(moe\.delivery\.[A-Za-z]+)=(.*?)\r?$/gm`, the way managed-vm.test.cjs parses its codes. Assert at least 14 entries and that no value contains a backslash (a properties escape this parser does not decode). Then deepStrictEqual the parsed object with a JSON round trip of DELIVERY_LABELS (title plus 13 row keys), and assert every corpus labelKey has a label. 3. `the task detail renders one escaped delivery row per expected entry`: render EVERY corpus row through the real panel with makeTask({ delivery: row.delivery }). Match rows across the HTML with step 3's markup contract, `/
([^<]*)<\/div>
([^<]*)<\/div><\/div>/g` (the architect dry-ran it in node). Compare each match, in order, with its expected entry: the outcome class (pass, fail or none), escapeHtml(DELIVERY_LABELS[labelKey]), escapeHtml(fullValue) and escapeHtml(value). The test's escapeHtml is a local copy of the panel's five replacements (& < > " '). A row with entries holds `
Delivery
` exactly once, inside `id="deliverySection"`. A row with an empty expect (D01 null, D06 empty strings) holds neither `id="deliverySection"` nor `delivery-row`. Also assert that D07's raw `npm test` never appears unescaped, and that the page's style block defines the `.delivery-pass` and `.delivery-fail` selectors.

implementationPlan.description:
Types and the presentation port.
- In moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts, add a type-only `TaskDelivery` interface mirroring packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.ts, with every member optional: currentCandidate {id, treeSha, shortSha, baseRevision}, latestCheckRun {command, exitCode, source, outcome}, requiredCheckSatisfied, deliveryReceipt {target, landedRevision}, attemptPhase. Add `delivery?: TaskDelivery | null` to Task, with a comment that the daemon serves it on /ws and the raw client passes it through untouched, like the blocker fields.
- In moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts, add these exports next to the blocker presentation block. Keep them inside the file with no new value import (mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map):
  - `DeliveryOutcome = 'PASS' | 'FAIL'`;
  - `DeliveryRow { labelKey: string; value: string; fullValue: string; outcome: DeliveryOutcome | null }`;
  - `DELIVERY_TITLE_KEY = 'moe.delivery.title'`;
  - `DELIVERY_LABELS: Record<string, string>`, the 14 moe.delivery.* entries copied exactly from moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties lines 258-271;
  - `deliveryRows(delivery: unknown): DeliveryRow[]`, a port of moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt plus MoeJson.parseDelivery's type guards, because VS Code receives raw wire JSON.
- deliveryRows rules:
  - Anything but a non-null, non-array object gives []. currentCandidate, latestCheckRun and deliveryReceipt get the same guard.
  - A text member counts only as a non-empty string; anything else is absent, never coerced or thrown on.
  - Row order: candidateSha, candidateBase, checkCommand, exit verdict, checkOutcome, checkSource, required-check verdict, receiptTarget, landedRevision, attemptPhase.
  - candidateSha is treeSha when that is a non-empty string, else shortSha. An empty treeSha must fall back: a bare `??` would keep it (corpus D04).
  - SHA rows (candidateSha, candidateBase, landedRevision) show value.slice(0, 8) and keep the full fullValue. Every other row has fullValue === value. outcome is null unless stated below.
  - The exit verdict renders only when exitCode is a number that passes Number.isSafeInteger (the daemon's store contract; strings are never coerced). It passes iff code === 0 and the outcome is absent, empty or exactly 'passed': moe.delivery.checkPassed PASS. Otherwise a non-zero code gives moe.delivery.checkFailed FAIL, and exit 0 with any other outcome gives moe.delivery.checkNotPassed FAIL. The value is String(code).
  - checkOutcome is shown verbatim, never whitelisted (anything but 'passed' fails closed). checkSource shows only 'runner-observed' or 'agent-reported'.
  - requiredCheckSatisfied === true gives moe.delivery.requiredCheckCounted 'yes' PASS; === false gives moe.delivery.requiredCheckNotCounted 'no' FAIL; anything else gives no row.
- Error handling: deliveryRows never throws on malformed input; every failed guard means "no row", as in JetBrains.
implementationPlan.note: Added the type-only TaskDelivery plus Task.delivery?: TaskDelivery | null to moe.ts. Added DeliveryOutcome, DeliveryRow, DELIVERY_TITLE_KEY, DELIVERY_LABELS (14 entries, copied from MoeBundle.properties) and deliveryRows (port of DeliveryPresentation.rows + MoeJson guards; non-empty-string guard so an empty treeSha falls back; Number.isSafeInteger exit codes; never throws) to TaskDetailPanel.ts. No new import. Edit tool only. Peers' dirty paths untouched.

Added private renderDelivery (exact markup contract: div.delivery-section#deliverySection > div.section-title + div.delivery-row[.delivery-pass|.delivery-fail] > div.field-label + div.delivery-value[title=fullValue]; every string via escapeHtml; '' when no rows), called directly after #blockerSection and before the editable fields, plus the 4 CSS rules next to .blocker-text. media/taskDetail.js untouched. Edit tool only.

Error handling for a red run:

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: deliveryRows takes the raw wire object (unknown) and carries MoeJson's type guards itself, because VS Code has no parser layer, so the same corpus bytes drive both clients. Exit codes follow the daemon contract (Number.isSafeInteger) rather than JetBrains' Int range. The corpus does not pin out-of-Int codes, and JetBrains dropping them is a recorded JetBrains gap (mem:decision-client-corpus-conventions). Rejected: re-rendering the whole HTML on every state change for live refresh, which would lose unsaved edits and the scroll position. Deferred: live refresh through media/taskDetail.js, which is not in this DoD and is a file VSC-11 owns; noted on VSC-18. The pinned single-line markup lets the test match rows by regex without a DOM parser.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Panels load under node:vm with strict require maps and strict client proxies (three peer tests), so helpers stay inside TaskDetailPanel.ts. vm-realm return values fail deepStrictEqual on prototypes; round-trip them through JSON first. The webview CSP allows inline styles. The initial HTML is built once in the constructor, and later updates go through postMessage to media/taskDetail.js.
planningNotes.risks: TaskDetailPanel.ts is shared with VSC-9 and VSC-11; in shared-checkout mode do not run concurrently with them. The corpus is held out: a corpus edit is an automatic QA reject. The snapshot must be the WHOLE repo, because the test reads moe-jetbrains files. A HEAD carrying a peer's red wip checkpoint can turn the full gate red (mem:gotcha-snapshot-gate-peer-wip-checkpoint). The test count grows as peers land tests, so compare against the baseline and name the new file's count.
